**Finding submitted: deviation (WARRANTY).**

**What I found**

- **§9 "TRUELINK WARRANTIES" (p0059–p0060)** is the only Vendor-side warranty, and it is limited entirely to **Y2K date processing**. It says nothing about workmanlike performance, conformance to documentation, compliance with laws, or malicious code, and provides no repair/replace/refund remedy.
- Those protections run only in the *opposite* direction: **Client** warrants compliance with laws (p0051) and that Client Content is free of viruses and malicious code (p0056).
- **§12 (p0076)** disclaims all implied warranties of merchantability and fitness for purpose, so with no express quality warranty the Client is left effectively unprotected — short of walk-away only because the disclaimer is not a full "AS IS."
- No conformance, specification, or documentation warranty exists anywhere else (searches for "conform," "Specifications," "Documentation," "professional and workmanlike" returned nothing relevant).

This fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies) on a material term.

**Redline (validated ok:true)** — inserted after p0060, at the preferred position: workmanlike performance of Hosting/Support Services; 12-month conformance for the Interface and related software; 90-day conformance for services; compliance with laws; no malicious code; with a re-performance/repair/replacement/refund remedy at TrueLink's option.

**Two points worth noting for the negotiation:**
1. No carve-out edit to §12 was needed — the disclaimer opens with "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so it will not swallow the new express warranty. This kept the edit minimal.
2. The remedy sits outside the §12 liability cap's enumerated sections (p0077 caps only Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11), so the refund remedy should not be independently capped — but confirm this if the section numbering shifts.
